title: Prime-complement generators, minimal neighborhoods, and localized units
statement:
Let $P$ be a fine commutative monoid, written additively, and let $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ be any finite tuple of monoid generators, allowing $r=0$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal in $X=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P$, and put
$$F=P\setminus\mathfrak p,\qquad I=\{i:e_i\in F\},\qquad b=\sum_{i\in I}e_i,$$
with empty sum $0$. The submonoid $F$ is a face: if $c+d\in F$, then $c,d\in F$. Every expression of an element of $F$ as a sum of generators uses only generators in $F$, and $F$ is generated by the $e_i$ with $i\in I$.
One has
$$D(b)=\bigcap_{i\in I}D(e_i)=\bigcap_{f\in F}D(f).$$
The open $D(b)$ contains $\mathfrak p$ and is contained in every open neighborhood of $\mathfrak p$. Inside $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ one has $P_b=P-F$; for every $i\in I$, the inverse of $e_i$ in $P_b$ is $(b-e_i)-b$, where $b-e_i$ denotes the sum of the other selected generators. Finally, for each $p\in P$,
$$p\in(P-F)^\times\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists q\in P,\ f\in F,\ p+q=f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p\in F.$$
Here units and localizations have the meanings in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]; the equalities $p+q=f$ are equalities in $P$, not merely in its group completion.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.4(i)--(iii), printed p.98: finite-generator localization at a point and units in a face localization; old proof steps 6 and 8.

proof.text: By [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], a prime ideal is proper and its complement is closed under addition. Since $0\in\mathfrak p$ would imply $\mathfrak p=P$ by the ideal property, $0\in F$. If $c+d\in F$ but $c\in\mathfrak p$, the ideal property gives $c+d\in\mathfrak p$, a contradiction; interchange $c,d$ for the other implication. Thus $F$ is a face.

source.place: VIII 3.1.3, p.98: prime ideals and complements

proof.text: Induct on membership in the closure of the given generators, with the assertion that any expression outside the prime lies in the closure of the selected generators. For a product outside the prime, step 1 puts both factors outside it, so the induction hypotheses multiply. The generator and identity cases are immediate. Conversely the selected generators, and hence their closure, lie in the complementary submonoid. A finite product outside the prime has every factor outside it; splitting a positive power gives the assertion about nonzero exponents.

source.place: VIII 3.1.2--3.1.4(ii), p.98: expand the finite-generation argument

proof.text:
For any prime $\mathfrak q$, its complement is a face by the argument of step 1. Consequently $b
otin\mathfrak q$ if and only if $e_i
otin\mathfrak q$ for every $i\in I$. By step 2 these conditions are equivalent to $f
otin\mathfrak q$ for every $f\in F$. Applying the definition of $D$ gives both displayed open-set equalities. When $I=\varnothing$, $b=0$, $D(0)=X$, and the empty intersection is $X$.

The product b avoids the original prime by complement multiplication. For any other prime q in D(b), step 3 says every element outside the original prime also avoids q. Thus every generating open D(f) containing the original prime contains q. Induct on the generated topology: the same property is preserved by the whole space, binary intersections, and arbitrary unions. Every open neighborhood of the original prime therefore contains D(b).

Since b belongs to the complementary submonoid, powers of b belong to it, giving P_b contained in P-F. Prove by closure induction on selected generators that every f in F has f*q=b^n for some q in P and natural n. For a selected generator use the product of the other indexed generators and n=1; for the identity use q=1,n=0; multiply witnesses and add exponents for products. Then p/f=(p*q)/b^n in the group completion, proving the reverse inclusion without choosing a maximum of exponents.

source.place: VIII 3.1.2 and 3.1.4(iii), p.98: localization at one element

proof.text: For $i\in I$, put $h_i=\sum_{j\in I,\ j\ne i}e_j\in P$. Then $h_i+e_i=b$, so $h_i-b\in P_b$ and $e_i+(h_i-b)=0$ in $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. By the unit definition in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] this is the required inverse $(b-e_i)-b$. The sum omits one index, so repeated generators cause no problem.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98: explicit inverse in the localization

proof.text: If $p\in P$ is a unit of $P-F$, its inverse has the form $q-f$ with $q\in P$, $f\in F$. The equality $p+(q-f)=0$ gives $p+q=f$ in $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$, hence in $P$ because fineness includes injectivity of $P\to P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. Conversely such an equality makes $q-f$ an inverse. Finally $p+q=f\in F$ implies $p\in F$ by step 1, while for $p\in F$ choose $q=0$, $f=p$. This proves both equivalences.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98: units and integral localization
